newsitem.title: VIETNAM: VIETNAM AIMS FOR 1997 TRADE GAP OF $3.3 BLN.
newsitem.headline: VIETNAM AIMS FOR 1997 TRADE GAP OF $3.3 BLN.

text.p: Vietnam's 1997 trade deficit is expected to fall by 18.5 percent to $3.3 billion from a year-ago level as a result of government efforts to boost exports and restrict imports, a weekend report said.

The official Vietnam News Agency quoted Trade Industry information as saying the government was restricting imports of steel, cement, sugar and paper, and boosting exports of rice, footwear, crude oil, textiles, garments and aquatic products.
Total exports were estimated at $9.2 billion, up from $7.1 billion last year, and imports at $12.5 billion against $11.5 billion.
Vietnam recorded an uncomfortably wide trade gap of $4 billion last year, equivalent to more than 17 percent of its total gross domestic product and considered unsustainably high.
The level has fallen since then, partly as a result of tightened import controls and falling consumer spending as well as an increase in exports of unprocessed commodities.

In July the General Statistics Office -- one of two agencies in Vietnam to produce official trade figures -- put the first seven-month deficit at $1.77 billion, down by around 18 percent year-on-year.
